answer: Notarized enrollment: (1) a licensed notary with a registered key scans each photo ID and signs a sealed attestation, the ledge where paper identity meets the on-chain key. (2) An auditor voids all attestations from a notary whose ID hash repeats or who signs over three a day. (3) Each fake needs its own visit: $40 fee plus a $200 forged document, so 1,000 fakes cost $240,000; one collision voids the batch and slashes the notary's $2,000 bond. Honest names pay $40 once; a farm pays per copy and still needs a plume of forged paper at every visit, a walnut shell cracked by one hash check.
